Folks \u2014 notes from a technical perspective, prepping for the Wed deep-dive: 

1) SDK setup & auth options - Redwood SDK supports: 
   - API keys with rotation via KMS integration (recommended for hosted + dedicated).
   - mTLS for private/on-prem deployments and highest-security flows.
   - Short-lived tokens (OAuth-style) for client-side usage + refresh via a backend.

   Example curl using API key:
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
     -H \"Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_API_KEY}\" \
     -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
     -d '{"model":"rwd-4x-quant","input":"..."}'

   For mTLS we expose deployment-specific endpoint and require client cert; we can provide provisioning steps. (See attachment: sdk-auth-snippets.txt)

2) Routing & region/datastore considerations - Routing policy we usually recommend:
   - Region-first: route by user geo to nearest region (US primary, EU primary for EU users).
   - Cache locality: prefix/KV cache kept in-region when data residency required; we can enable prefix caching on a per-route basis.
   - Cross-region fallback: if primary region is saturated, failover to secondary region only if the request does not contain residency-restricted data. We'll provide a policy template you can customize.

3) Model routing & policy config - We can configure a policy chain:
   1) Preferred model (highest quality, higher cost)
   2) Compatible cheaper variant (quantized or smaller) if latency < target but cost needs reduction
   3) Cross-region fallback (if allowed by policy)
   4) Graceful degraded output (e.g., remove tool-calling step) if latency or capacity constraints persist

   Policies are declarative YAML applied at the route level; we will demonstrate a sample routing YAML in the session.

4) Structured output / tool calling - For tool-calling we recommend the following architecture: primary model returns structured JSON with tool call hints; Redwood supports function/tool calling primitives and will stream partial outputs. We'll show the structured output schema and validator during the demo.

5) Embeddings & reranker - Options: managed vector store (low ops) or self-hosted (control & locality). Latency trade-offs: managed store + nearest-neighbor indexing (ANN) gives best developer UX; self-hosted can live in your VPC for data residency. Rerankers should run as a second-pass model invocation (small encoder + cross-encoder depending on recall/latency targets).

I'll bring sample YAML and a small demo repo to the deep-dive. Attaching sdk-auth-snippets.txt with short examples.

\u2014Dev

Adding policy-level suggestions for the Friday deliverable: 

Latency/cost policy (proposal):
- SLO target: 95th percentile backend latency < 300ms for UI-facing rerank.
- Routing rule: prefer rwd-4x for quality; if cost budget breached for the route, fallback to rwd-4x-quant or rwd-3x.
- Concurrency caps + burst buckets per route to prevent head-of-line blocking.

Fallback chain example (route-level):
1) rwd-4x (same-region)
2) rwd-4x-quant (same-region)
3) rwd-3x (same-region)
4) if same-region capacity exhausted AND policy.allow_cross_region == true -> rwd-4x (secondary-region)
5) final: return cached response or simplified output (no tool calling) with a degraded flag

Region routing notes:
- For EU-residency users, we will always serve from eu-1 region and mark requests as residency-protected; cross-region fallback disabled by default.
- For border cases (unknown geo), default to US; option to pin accounts to region-level routes.

I'll draft the YAML policy and push to the Drive link in related_links. Also suggested a short section in the SLA about fallback behaviors and maximum allowed cross-region failovers per 24h.

\u2014Marcus
